lines.text: A king made his enemies carry river water.
All the way from the Ganges, to the Tamil country.
His name was Rajendra Chola, son of the builder of Thanjavur.
Around the year ten twenty five, he founded a new capital.
He called it Gangaikonda Cholapuram. The city of the Chola who took the Ganga.
The temple here was finished in about ten thirty five.
A royal praise inscription says defeated rulers carried Ganga water, in pots.
It was poured into a new water body, called Chola Gangam. A victory pillar, made of water.
Historians note this is the king's own boast. No one else recorded the ceremony.
Tradition says its tower was built a little lower, out of respect for his father.
Around it, a whole city once stood. Palaces, walls, a fort.
Today, only mounds, brick walls, and broken pillars remain.
Why the city fell is unclear. Some point to Pandya revenge. Others, to raids from Delhi.
Yet the temple survived, and people still worship there.
A thousand years on, the king's boast still stands in stone.
Follow Aazhi for the next chronicle.
